title: Course Schedule
prompt:
There are `numCourses` courses (0 to numCourses-1). `prerequisites[i] = [a, b]` means you must take course `b` before course `a`. Return whether it's possible to finish all courses.

This is cycle detection in a directed graph — Kahn's topological sort: if peeling zero-prerequisite courses can consume the whole graph, there's no cycle.
hints: Edge direction: b → a (prerequisite points to dependent). indegree[a]++ per pair.
Queue every course with indegree 0; poll, count it, decrement neighbors' indegrees, enqueue those that hit 0.
All courses processed ⟺ no cycle ⟺ return processed == numCourses.

solution.explanation: Kahn's algorithm, O(V + E). Courses inside a cycle never reach indegree 0, so they're never processed — the final count exposes them. (Course Schedule II is the same code returning the poll order.)
